data.hypothesis: Combining the prior invariant hoisting with local per-pixel accumulation may reduce repeated scalar setup and channel read-modify-writes, but the isolated results do not imply an additive gain: hoisting was only marginally faster than baseline, while accumulation alone was slower. The ordered float additions, primary-ray generation, AO kernel, RNG sequence, and scheduling remain unchanged; the controller should test the combination for all correctness cases and repeated timings.

memory_lessons.applicability: Scalar primary-path changes in this campaign; compiler-generated hoisting and interaction with output updates can mask or reverse expected benefits.
memory_lessons.claim: The invariant-hoisting candidate was valid at 3.4936 s versus the 3.4961 s baseline, while local accumulation alone was valid at 3.5263 s. These close results do not establish a reliable hoisting speedup or predict the combination's performance.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the combined candidate with the same correctness cases and repeated timing protocol; compare directly with the original and both isolated candidates.

data.notes: This candidate combines the two previously isolated transformations. The supplied records report all six correctness cases passing for the baseline and both isolated candidates. No new correctness or timing run is claimed here; the combined candidate still needs the controller's official correctness checks, repeated timings, and threshold evaluation.
transformations: Hoist float half-width, half-height, aspect ratio, and subsample-count conversion to per-call setup while retaining the original primary-coordinate arithmetic order.
Accumulate each primary-ray result into one local float per pixel in the original subsample traversal order.
Normalize the accumulated scalar once and write the same resulting value to each of the three image channels once per pixel.
Leave AO ray generation/intersection, geometry, RNG calls and sequence, primary sample count/order, and serial scheduling unchanged.
